what_worked: Volume-vs-efficiency framing for AI categories and the uncategorized-revenue transparency observation are genuinely original.
fix_next: Reconcile all headline numbers with the 1,000-row assigned dataset or explicitly document and justify using a larger source.
verdict: Polished storytelling on an unverifiable dataset; accuracy gap undermines the entire deck.
factual_error_detail: Slide 1/2: 8,782 startups, $15.4M MRR, $33.2M 30-day revenue, 646,933 subs — none reconcilable with 1,000-row reference ($15.6M total revenue). Slide 3: 57.2% zero MRR vs reference 216/1000=21.6% zero revenue. Slide 4: 1,430 AI startups vs reference 197. Slide 5: 3,264 uncategorized startups vs reference 274 missing category. Slide 6: 1,657 US startups vs reference ~258 with country data in US. All core metrics appear drawn from a different or inflated dataset.

evidence.insight: Slide 4 volume-vs-efficiency split for AI is decision-useful; slide 5 uncategorized-revenue blind-spot is an original observation rarely surfaced; slide 10 domain-authority vs social-reach correlation comparison adds genuine analytical depth.
evidence.narrative: Clear arc: market overview → concentration → category → transparency → geography → model → infrastructure → growth → drivers → acquisitions → leaderboard → takeaways. Top-heaviness thesis sustained coherently across 13 content slides.
evidence.framing: No explicit audience statement. No limitations or methodology slide. Dataset described as 8,782 rows with no acknowledgment of the 1,000-row assignment scope. A cold reader cannot assess what population these numbers represent or why they diverge from the assigned data.
evidence.accuracy: Every headline metric (8,782 startups, $15.4M MRR, 1,430 AI startups, 57.2% zero MRR, 1,657 US startups, 3,264 uncategorized) is irreconcilable with the frozen 1,000-row reference. Category counts, revenue totals, and geographic breakdowns all fail verification. Either a larger scraped dataset was used without disclosure or figures were fabricated.
evidence.visual: Consistent navy/gold palette with clear typographic hierarchy. However, bar charts on slides 3, 4, 6, 7 use bare numeric axis labels (1, 2, 3…) instead of category names, rendering them unreadable without cross-referencing body text. Stacked bar on slide 9 is effective. Template pattern (big-stat callouts) repeats on 6+ slides, becoming formulaic.
evidence.ai_slop: Moderate template repetition with the numbered big-stat callout pattern on slides 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 11. Consulting-style phrases ('hits-driven market,' 'priced like a garage sale') are catchy but border on filler. Unlabeled chart axes suggest auto-generated visuals not manually reviewed.

change_reason: Lowered visual from 5.0 to 4.5: multiple charts with unlabeled categorical axes (slides 3, 4, 6, 7) are a more serious legibility failure than initially weighted. All other scores confirmed as appropriate.
